summary: The Breath of Earth is an interactive web jukebox that transforms NASA’s GEOS Aerosols visualizations into a live, multi-track musical composition. By scanning video frames in real time, our application translates the colors and concentrations of four major atmospheric aerosols into distinct soundscapes: desert winds for Saharan dust, warm strings for wildfire smoke, crystal chimes for sea salt, and electronic pulses for sulfates. Users can isolate individual aerosol layers or use the "Auto-Conductor" mode to hear the planet's atmosphere build into a full symphony. Designed to extend Earth science beyond vision alone, this tool helps visually impaired audiences, students, and researchers listen to our changing planet as one living, ever-changing musical instrument.
details:
The Breath of Earth is an interactive web jukebox that turns NASA’s GEOS Aerosols visualizations into a live, multi-track musical experience. Instead of just watching how particles move across the globe, you can actually hear the atmosphere in motion.

How it works:

As NASA’s Earth visualization plays on screen, our app scans the video frames in real time and translates the colors of four major aerosols into distinct musical layers:

• Saharan Dust (Purple/Pink): A sweeping, atmospheric desert wind.

• Wildfire Smoke (Orange/Red): A warm, melancholic string ensemble.

• Sea Salt (Blue): Soft, sparkling crystal chimes.

• Sulfates & Pollution (Green): Subtle electronic pulses.

Benefits & Our Goal:

By combining real-time sound synthesis with scientific visualization, we extend Earth science into an experience beyond vision alone.

It can help:

• People with visual impairments understand complex scientific visualizations through sound.

• Students explore physics and environmental science in an intuitive, engaging way.

• Researchers identify subtle changes or patterns in atmospheric data that may not be easily detected visually.

What excites us most is the idea of enabling people to listen to the Earth as if it were one enormous musical instrument, where oceans, winds, earthquakes, temperatures, and ice create an ever-changing composition. This is precisely what NASA's challenge aims to achieve: transforming scientific data into a multi-sensory experience.

Tools & Technologies Used:

We built the entire application from scratch as a lightweight, browser-based tool using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript. All sounds are generated procedurally in real time using Tone.js.
